extracted.intended_audience: graduate or advanced undergraduate students and researchers studying category theory / mathematicians learning about limits and adjoint functor theorems
extracted.subtask_description: Formal statements, definitions, and constructive criteria for existence, formation, preservation, and creation of limits (and related notions like products, equalizers, projectives, adjoints, representability) in category theory. Includes the Freyd adjoint functor theorem and pointwise calculation of limits in functor categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — V creates limits for F
rubrics_metrics.description: A functor V: A -> X creates limits for a functor F : J -> A if (i) to every limiting cone c: x -> V F in X there is exactly one pair <a, λ> consisting of an object a in A with Va = x and a cone λ: a -> F with Vλ = c, and (ii) this cone λ: a -> F is a limiting cone in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notion generalizes to 'V creates products' (restrict J to discrete), 'V creates finite limits' (restrict J finite), and 'V creates colimits' (reverse arrows). Note: 'V creates limits' only applies when V F already has a limit in X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forgetful functors create limits (example/criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If U: Grp -> Set and U ∘ H has a limit L with limiting cone in Set, then there is exactly one group structure on the underlying set L making the cone morphisms group homomorphisms; thus the forgetful functor creates limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More generally, typical algebraic forgetful functors (Grp, Rng, Ab, R-Mod, varieties) create all small limits: the limit's underlying set is the limit in Set and algebraic operations are defined coordinatewise. This gives a constructive recipe for limits in algebraic categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits by products and equalizers — existence criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a category C has equalizers of all pairs of arrows and has all products indexed by obj(J) and arr(J), then C has limits for every functor F: J -> C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction proceeds by forming two products (one over objects of J, one over arrows of J), producing arrows f,g between these products, and then taking their equalizer e; the equalizer object with induced projections yields the limit cone. This gives a practical method to build limits from products and equalizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete formulation — limit as equalizer of two product-arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: The limit of F: J -> C is the equalizer e of f,g: ∏_{i∈obj(J)} F i -> ∏_{u∈arr(J)} F(codu), where the component maps are defined so that the limiting cone projections are P_j ∘ e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit description identifies the limiting cone as the subobject of the product satisfying all compatibility equations (Fu)∘P_j = P_k for each u:j→k. Use when constructing limits in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite completeness criterion (Corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: If C has a terminal object, equalizers of all pairs of arrows, and binary products (products of all pairs of objects), then C has all finite limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finite limits = limits of diagrams indexed by finite categories. Use the above product+equalizer recipe specialized to finite index categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-completeness criterion (Corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: If C has equalizers of all pairs of arrows and all small products, then C is small-complete (has all small limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows sufficiency of products + equalizers at the small (set-indexed) level for arbitrary small limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freyd proposition — structure of small-complete small categories
rubrics_metrics.description: A small category C which is small-complete is a preorder which has a greatest lower bound for every small set of its elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a necessary structural consequence: non-preorder small categories cannot be small-complete (argument via counting of arrows into products). Useful as a diagnostic: if C is small and not a preorder, it cannot have all small limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits with parameters — pointwise construction criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T: J×P -> X be a bifunctor. If for each p in P the functor T(-,p): J -> X has a limit L_p with limiting cone T_p, then the objects L_p assemble into a functor L: P -> X and the projections pr_p ∘ T_p together form a natural transformation T : L∘Δ -> S which is a limiting cone; i.e., limits depending on parameters assemble into a functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently: in functor categories, limits (when they exist pointwise) may be calculated pointwise. Use evaluation functors Ep to reduce to pointwise limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of limits — definition and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: A functor H: C -> D preserves limits of F: J -> C when composition gives that H applied to every limiting cone v: b -> F yields a limiting cone Hv: Hb -> H F in D. A functor is continuous if it preserves all small limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preservation requires both that H send limit objects to limit objects and that H take limiting cones to limiting cones (not merely up to isomorphism). 'Continuous' is the categorical analogue of continuity: preserves all small limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom-functors preserve limits (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If C has small hom-sets, then for any object c the hom-functor C(c,-): C -> Set preserves all limits (in particular, small limits). More generally if hom-sets live in an 'Ens' of sets of functions, the same holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses universality of the limit and the bijection Cone(X,S) ≅ Set(X, Lim S). Practical consequence: representability/adjunction computations can reduce limit questions to Set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation implies preservation (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If V: A -> X creates limits for F: J -> A and V F has a limit in X, then V preserves the limit of F (i.e., Va is a limit and V sends the limiting cone in A to the limiting cone in X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to deduce continuity of forgetful functors: if V creates all small limits and X is small-complete then A is small-complete and V is continuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective and injective objects — categorical criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An object p is projective exactly when every arrow h: p->c factors through every epi g: b->c (equivalently hom(p,-) preserves epis). Dually, q is injective when hom(-,q) carries monomorphisms to epimorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are especially useful in module categories; e.g., in R-Mod projectives are precisely direct summands of free modules. Characterize by lifting properties relative to epis/monos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right adjoints preserve limits (theorem/criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If G: A -> X has a left adjoint F, then G preserves all limits which exist in A: if τ: a -> T is limiting in A, then Gτ: Ga -> G T is limiting in X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via adjunction: cones in X correspond under adjunction to cones in A, and universality transfers. Dually, left adjoints preserve colimits. Use this to show standard forgetful functors preserve products, equalizers, kernels, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of initial object — solution set condition (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let D be small-complete with small hom-sets. D has an initial object iff there exists a small set I and an I-indexed family k_i of objects of D such that for every d in D there is some i in I and an arrow k_i -> d (the solution set condition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: take product of the k_i and equalize all its endomorphisms to produce an initial object. This solution set condition is necessary and sufficient for existence of initial objects in small-complete categories with small hom-sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freyd Adjoint Functor Theorem — existence of left adjoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be small-complete with small hom-sets. A functor G: A -> X has a left adjoint iff (1) G preserves all small limits and (2) for each x in X there is a small set I and an I-indexed family of arrows f_i: x -> G a_i such that every arrow h: x -> G a factors as h = G t ∘ f_i for some i and some t: a_i -> a (the solution set condition for G at x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The solution set condition provides smallness required to construct an initial object in the comma category (x ↓ G). Combined with preservation of limits, one constructs the universal arrow x -> G(Fx) pointwise, obtaining the left adjoint. Applications: constructions of free algebras (free group, free ring), Stone-Čech compactification (left adjoint to forgetful CompHaus -> Set), and left adjoints to forgetful functors for varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability criterion (Representability Theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let D be small-complete with small hom-sets. A functor K: D -> Set is representable iff K preserves all small limits and satisfies a solution set condition: there exists a small set S of objects of D such that for any d in D and any x in K d there exist s in S, y in K s and f: s -> d with K f(y) = x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: representability = existence of a universal element (initial object in (* ↓ K)); continuity and the solution set condition together are necessary and sufficient. Example shows continuity alone is not sufficient.
